about: This part finishes the seventh day and closes the peaceful bardo. Round the knowledge-holder of full ripening, who dawned at the end of the last part, the four knowledge-holders of the directions appear, each with a sky-goer consort, dancing with curved knife and skull of blood: Dwelling on the Levels in the east, white; Power over Life in the south, yellow; the Great Seal in the west, red; Spontaneous Presence in the north, green. Around them come countless sky-goers, heroes and heroines, ging and guardians of the teaching, in bone ornaments, with drums, thigh-bone trumpets and banners of skin, filling every world and shaking it, to welcome those who keep their vows and punish those who broke them. From the hearts of the five knowledge-holders a light of the five colours of coemergent wisdom, like twisted coloured threads, strikes the dead man's heart, and beside it dawns the dull green light of the animals. He is not to fear the bright light or its roar of a thousand thunders, nor to be drawn to the dull one, which leads to birth as a dumb beast; he is to turn to the knowledge-holders, lament that so many deities have held him and not caught him, and ask them to draw him to the Sky-Faring realm with the hook of their compassion, in a prayer of eight lines. Whoever makes it dissolves into their hearts as rainbow light. The text then says that all who have had a spiritual friend are freed here, and even those of bad tendencies, and closes: this was the Great Liberation through Hearing for the bardo of the moment of death and the peaceful bardo of reality. Iti; seal, seal, seal.

sentences.w: དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ དེའི་ ཤར་ ནས་ ས་ ལ་ གནས་པའི་ རིག་འཛིན་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ དཀར་ ཞིང་ འཛུམ་པའི་ མདངས་ དང་ ལྡན་པ༔ ཡུམ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་ དཀར་མོ་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་ ཞིང་ གྲི་གུག་ དང་ ཐོད་ཁྲག་ གི་ གར་ མཛད་ ཅིང་༔ བལྟ་སྟངས་ ཀྱི་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ ནམ་མཁའ་ ལ་ མཛད་པ་ ཅིག་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Maṇḍala that's east from, On-the-Levels Dwelling's knowledge-holder so-called, body-colour white and smiling's radiance with endowed, mother sky-goer white body to embracing and, curved-knife and skull-blood's dance making, and, gazing-manner's seal sky-to making, one, dawning comes.
sentences.i: From the east of that maṇḍala dawns the knowledge-holder called Dwelling on the Levels, his body white, with a smiling radiance; his consort, a white sky-goer, embraces him, and he dances with the curved knife and the skull full of blood, making the gesture of gazing toward the sky.
sentences.n: The four knowledge-holders of the directions, round the one of full ripening in the centre, who closed the last part; each has the same five phrases. sa la gnas pa'i, 'dwelling on the sa': sa is 'earth, ground', and also the word for the levels (Sanskrit bhūmi) of a bodhisattva's path, and the name is taken in that sense; 'Dwelling on the Earth' is the plain sense of the words. Four of the five names, full ripening (in the centre), power over life, the great seal and spontaneous presence, are elsewhere the usual list of the stages a knowledge-holder reaches; Dwelling on the Levels, the fifth here, is read with them, and the text itself does not explain the names. 'dzum pa'i mdangs, 'a smiling radiance'. yum mkha' 'gro dkar mo has mkha' 'gro without -ma, where the other three have mkha' 'gro ma; the sense is the same. 'khril zhing, 'embracing, and', where the others have 'khril ba. gri gug dang thod khrag gi gar mdzad, 'makes the dance of the curved knife and the skull of blood', the dance done with them in the hands; the next three vary the particle (gis 'with', gi again, 'dzin pas 'holding'). Who dances is not said; the knowledge-holder is taken. The other recension has lta stangs for blta stangs (007) here and in the next three.

sentences.w: དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ དེའི་ ལྷོ་ ནས་ ཚེ་ ལ་ དབང་བའི་ རིག་འཛིན་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ སེར་ ཞིང་ མཛེས་པའི་ དཔེ་བྱད་ དང་ ལྡན་བ༔ ཡུམ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་མ་ སེར་མོ་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གྲི་གུག་ དང་ ཐོད་ཁྲག་ གིས་ གར་ མཛད་ ཅིང་༔ བལྟ་སྟངས་ ཀྱི་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ ནམ་མཁའ་ ལ་ མཛད་པ་ གཅིག་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Maṇḍala that's south from, Life over Power's knowledge-holder so-called, body-colour yellow and beautiful's minor-marks with endowed, mother sky-goer-woman yellow body to embracing, curved-knife and skull-blood with dance making, and, gazing-manner's seal sky-to making, one, dawning comes.
sentences.i: From the south of that maṇḍala dawns the knowledge-holder called Power over Life, his body yellow, with the beautiful minor marks; his consort, a yellow sky-goer, embraces him; he dances with the curved knife and the skull full of blood, making the gesture of gazing toward the sky.
sentences.n: tshe la dbang ba, 'having power over life' (tshe, 'life'; dbang ba, 'to have power'), the knowledge-holder who has mastered his own lifespan. dpe byad, 'the minor marks', the eighty lesser signs of a buddha's body beside the thirty-two major ones; mdzes pa'i, 'beautiful'. sku mdog is doubtful on the image ([?]): the o-stroke of mdog stands where the tail of a letter on the line above also reaches; it is read as the vowel, which the sense needs (the transcription of this print has mdag, no word). ldan ba is the print's spelling of ldan pa, and gcig, 'one', its spelling of cig, here only in the five phrases; both are kept. gis, 'with, by', where the first had gi.

sentences.w: དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ དེའི་ ནུབ་ ནས་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོའི་ རིག་འཛིན་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ དམར་ ཞིང་ འཛུམ་པའི་ མདངས་ དང་ ལྡན་པ༔ ཡུམ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་མ་ དམར་མོ་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གྲི་གུག་ དང་ ཐོད་ཁྲག་ གི་ གར་ མཛད་ ཅིང་༔ བལྟ་སྟངས་ ཀྱི་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ ནམ་མཁའ་ ལ་ མཛད་པ་ ཅིག་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Maṇḍala that's west from, Great-Seal's knowledge-holder so-called, body-colour red and smiling's radiance with endowed, mother sky-goer-woman red body to embracing, curved-knife and skull-blood's dance making, and, gazing-manner's seal sky-to making, one, dawning comes.
sentences.i: From the west of that maṇḍala dawns the knowledge-holder called the Great Seal, his body red, with a smiling radiance; his consort, a red sky-goer, embraces him; he dances with the curved knife and the skull full of blood, making the gesture of gazing toward the sky.
sentences.n: phyag rgya chen po, 'the great seal' (Sanskrit mahāmudrā), the name of the highest realisation in several schools; here the knowledge-holder who has reached it. The words are those of the east, with red for white, mkha' 'gro ma for mkha' 'gro, and 'khril ba for 'khril zhing.

sentences.w: དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ དེའི་ བྱང་ ནས་ ལྷུན་གྱིས་གྲུབ་པའི་ རིག་འཛིན་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ ལྗང་ ཞིང་ ཞལ་ ཁྲོ་འཛུམ་ དང་ ལྡན་པ༔ ཡུམ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་མ་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གྲི་གུག་ དང་ ཐོད་ཁྲག་ འཛིན་པས་ གར་ མཛད་ ཅིང་༔ བལྟ་སྟངས་ ཀྱི་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ ནམ་མཁའ་ ལ་ མཛད་པ་ ཅིག་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Maṇḍala that's north from, Spontaneously-Present's knowledge-holder so-called, body-colour green and face wrathful-smiling with endowed, mother sky-goer-woman green body to embracing, curved-knife and skull-blood holding-by dance making, and, gazing-manner's seal sky-to making, one, dawning comes.
sentences.i: From the north of that maṇḍala dawns the knowledge-holder called Spontaneous Presence, his body green, his face both wrathful and smiling; his consort, a green sky-goer, embraces him; holding the curved knife and the skull full of blood he dances, making the gesture of gazing toward the sky.
sentences.n: lhun gyis grub pa, 'spontaneously present' (006). zhal, 'face', the respectful word; khro 'dzum, 'wrathful and smiling' (khro, 'wrath'; 'dzum, 'smile'), a face that is both at once. ljang khu, 'green'; the print runs ljang khu and sku together with no tsheg, here divided. 'dzin pas, 'by holding', where the others have gi or gis.

sentences.w: རིག་འཛིན་ དེ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱི་ རོལ་དུ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་མའི་ ཚོགས་ དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་ དང་༔ དུར་ཁྲོད་ བརྒྱད་ ཀྱི་ མཁའ་འགྲོ༔ རིགས་ བཞིའི་ མཁའ་འགྲོ༔ གནས་ གསུམ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ༔ གནས་ བཅུའི་ མཁའ་འགྲོ༔ ཡུལ་ ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་བཞིའི་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་ རྣམས་ དང་༔ དཔའ་བོ་ དང་༔ དཔའ་མོ་ དང་༔ གིང་ དང་༔ ཆོས་སྐྱོང་བའི་ བསྲུང་མ་ དང་ བཅས་པ་ ཐམས་ཅད་ རུས་པའི་ རྒྱན་ དྲུག་ གསོལ་ ནས༔
sentences.l: Knowledge-holders those (plural)'s side-at(?), sky-goer-women's hosts measure-to without and; charnel-grounds eight's sky-goers; families four's sky-goers; places three sky-goers; places ten's sky-goers; lands twenty-four's sky-goers (plural) and; heroes and; heroines and; ging and; dharma-protecting's guardians with together, all, bone's ornaments six wearing, then,
sentences.i: Around those knowledge-holders are hosts of sky-goers beyond measure: the sky-goers of the eight charnel grounds, of the four families, of the three places, of the ten places and of the twenty-four lands, with heroes and heroines, ging, and the guardians who protect the teaching. All of them wear the six bone ornaments,
sentences.n: The print has དབག (dbag), a misprint for དཔག (dpag), corrected here: dpag tu med pa, 'immeasurable', as the print itself writes it three lines below. The print has མཁའ་གྲོ (mkha' gro), a misprint for མཁའ་འགྲོ (mkha' 'gro), corrected here: the a-chung is dropped, and the word stands four more times in the same list. rnams kyi rol du is kept as printed: rol is 'side', so 'on their side, round them', but the usual word is phyi rol, 'outside'; the other recension has phyi rim du, 'in the outer ring', and the sense is about the same. The lists are of sacred places where sky-goers live: dur khrod brgyad, 'the eight charnel grounds'; rigs bzhi, 'the four families'; gnas gsum, gnas bcu and yul nyi shu rtsa bzhi, 'the three places, the ten places, the twenty-four lands', the sacred sites of the tantras. What the four families and the three and ten places are, the text does not say. dpa' bo and dpa' mo, 'heroes' and 'heroines' (dpa' bo, Sanskrit vīra), in the tantras the male and female companions of the sky-goers. ging, a class of wild dancing attendants in the retinue of the wrathful deities; the word is left untranslated. chos skyong ba'i bsrung ma, 'guardians who protect the teaching'; the other recension srung ma. dang bcas pa thams cad, 'all of them, together with'. rus pa'i rgyan drug, 'the six ornaments of bone' worn by tantric figures; gsol, the respectful 'wear'. The transcription of this print skips dpa' bo dang, which is on the image, as in the other recension.

sentences.w: རྔ་ དང་༔ རྐང་དུང་ དང་༔ ཐོད་རྔ་ དང་༔ ཞིང་ལྤགས་ ཀྱི་ རྒྱལ་མཚན་ དང་༔ མི་ལྤགས་ ཀྱི་ བླ་བྲེས་ དང་༔ མི་ལྤགས་ ཀྱི་ འཕན་ དང་༔ མི་གསུར་ གྱི་ དུད་པ་ དང་༔ རོལ་མོའི་ བྱེ་བྲག་ དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་ དང་ བཅས་ཏེ༔ འཇིག་རྟེན་ གྱི་ ཁམས་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཁེངས་པ་ ཤིག་ཤིག༔ ཡོམ་ཡོམ་ འགུལ་འགུལ་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: drums and; thigh-bone-trumpets and; skull-drums and; corpse-skin(?)'s victory-banners and; human-skin's canopies and; human-skin's pennants and; human-burnt-offering's smoke and; music's kinds measure-to without with together, and: world's realms all filling, shaking-shaking, swaying-swaying, quivering-quivering-ly come.
sentences.i: and with drums, thigh-bone trumpets and skull drums, banners of flayed skin, canopies and pennants of human skin, the smoke of burnt offerings of human flesh, and music of countless kinds, they come, filling all the realms of the world, shaking, swaying and quivering.
sentences.n: Each thing they bring is a noun with dang, 'and', and a ༔. rnga, 'drum'; rkang dung, 'thigh-bone trumpet' (rkang, 'leg-bone'; dung, 'horn'); thod rnga, 'skull drum', a small double-headed drum made of skulls. zhing lpags: lpags is 'skin'; zhing, 'field', is in tantric speech also the body of an enemy to be slain, and the word is taken as a flayed skin of that kind; the sense is not sure. rgyal mtshan, 'victory banner'. mi lpags, 'human skin'. mi[?]: an ink blot covers the vowel on the image, and mi is read as in the two words after it. bla bres, 'canopy' (the other recension bla re). 'phan, 'pennant'. gsur is a burnt offering, flour and food burnt for its smoke; mi gsur, 'a burnt offering of human (flesh)', taken so, with dud pa, 'smoke'. rol mo'i bye brag, 'kinds of music'. khengs pa, 'filling, filled'. shig shig, yom yom, 'gul 'gul: three doubled words of motion, 'shaking', 'swaying', 'quivering'; du, 'in the manner of', joins them to 'ong. The print sets ༔ after shig shig; the other recension has khengs par phyed༔ shig shig yom yom, with phyed, 'half', and the ༔ a word earlier.

sentences.w: རོལ་མོའི་ སྒྲ་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཀྱང་ མགོ་ འགས་པ་ ཙམ་ འདིར་བ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Music's sounds all also, head splitting as-much-as booming(?) come.
sentences.i: All the sounds of their music come booming loud enough to split one's head.
sentences.n: mgo 'gas pa tsam, 'as much as a head splitting' ('gas, 'to split, crack'): so loud that it would split the head. tsam 'dir ba is kept as printed. 'dir ba is taken as the verb ldir, 'to boom, roar', which the print has twice two pages on (76), spelt ldir; the print wrote 'dir for ldir in 003 too ('dir btsam du, taken there as ldir ba tsam du); the other recension has tsam du ldir nas 'ong ngo, 'come booming so loud that'. 'dir is also 'here', which would give 'come here', and less sense.

sentences.w: གར་ སྣ་ཚོགས་ བྱེད་ ཅིང་ དམ་ཚིག་ཅན་ རྣམས་ ཀྱི་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Dances various doing, and, commitment-holders (plural)'s meeting for come.
sentences.i: Performing many kinds of dance, they come to welcome those who keep their commitments.
sentences.n: byed[?], 'to do': the first letter could be b or ph on the image; the transcription has byed, the other recension phyed, 'half, to open', which gives no clear sense here. gar sna tshogs, 'dances of many kinds'. dam tshig can, 'one who has the commitment (dam tshig)', who keeps the vows of tantric practice; X kyi bsu ba la 'ong, 'come to meet X', as in 007; the other recension has bsu bar.

sentences.w: དམ་ཉམས་ རྣམས་ ལ་ ཆད་པ་ བཅད་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Commitment-broken (plural) to punishment cutting come.
sentences.i: Upon those whose commitments are broken they come to deal out punishment.
sentences.n: dam nyams, 'one whose commitment is broken' (007). chad pa gcod, 'to cut a punishment', the set phrase for imposing one; bcad is the past stem of gcod (gcod / bcad / gcad / chod), with du, 'to': 'come to impose'. Before du the future gcad would be expected; the other recension also has bcad du.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ བག་ཆགས་ དབྱིངས་སུ་ དག་པ་ ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ ཁ་དོག་ ལྔ་ དང་ ལྡན་པ༔ མཚོན་སྐུད་ སྒྲིལ་མ་ ལྟ་བུ༔ ཁྲ་ཤིག་ཤིག་པ༔ མེར་མེར་བ༔ ཕྱམ་ཕྱམ་པ༔ གཅིག་ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ༔ བཀྲག་ ལ་ ཉམ་ང་བ་ གཅིག༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Habitual-tendencies in-the-expanse purified, coemergent's wisdom's colours five with endowed, coloured-thread twisted like, mottled-shimmering, flickering, gleaming(?), one(?): bright and clear, lustrous and fearsome, one,
sentences.i: O child of noble family, the habitual tendencies purified in the expanse, a light of the five colours of coemergent wisdom, like twisted coloured threads, mottled and shimmering, flickering, gleaming, bright and clear, lustrous and fearsome,
sentences.n: The subject of a long phrase, whose verb comes in the next sentence; the print has no word for 'light' (the other recension has ye shes 'od kha dog lnga, 'a wisdom light of five colours'). bag chags dbyings su dag pa, 'habitual tendencies purified in the expanse', as on this day's first page (007). lhan cig skyes pa'i ye shes, 'coemergent wisdom' (lhan cig, 'together'; skyes pa, 'born'; Sanskrit sahaja), the wisdom born together with the mind itself. mtshon skud is taken as tshon skud, 'coloured thread' (tshon, 'colour, dye'; skud, 'thread'), which the other recension has; mtshon is 'weapon' or 'sign'. sgril ma, 'twisted, rolled'. Three doubled-sound words for the play of the light, their senses approximate: khra shig shig pa, khra 'mottled, many-coloured' with shig shig 'quivering'; mer mer ba, 'flickering', as flames do; phyam phyam pa, taken as 'gleaming', not sure. gcig, 'one', after them belongs with the words before: the other recension has phyam phyam pa zhig, 'a gleaming one', and the print's ༔ falls a word early; the translation leaves it out. gsal la dwangs pa, bkrag la nyam nga ba, 'bright and clear, lustrous and fearsome', as on the days before (gsal la dwangs pa in 004–006, bkrag la nyam nga ba'i in 007). The print has ཀྱཻ, the other recension ཀྱེ.

sentences.w: རིགས་འཛིན་ གྱི་ གཙོ་བོ་ ལྔའི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཐད་ སྙིང་ཀར་ མིག་ གིས་ མི་ བཟོད་པ་ ཙམ་དུ་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Knowledge-holders' chiefs five's heart from, you-yourself's straight heart-at, eye by not bearable as-much-as piercing, comes.
sentences.i: comes from the heart of the five chief knowledge-holders and strikes straight into your heart, so bright that the eye cannot bear it.
sentences.n: rigs 'dzin is the print's spelling, here only, of rig 'dzin. gtso bo, 'chief'; gtso bo lnga, 'the five chiefs', the five knowledge-holders just described. thad snying kar: thad, 'straight at', with snying kar, 'at the heart'; the other recension has snying gi thad kar, 'straight at the heart', the same sense. mig gis mi bzod pa tsam du, 'so much that the eye cannot bear it'; the other recension has mig gis lta mi bzod pa, 'that the eye cannot bear to look at'. zug nas 'ong, 'comes piercing', as on the days before.

sentences.w: དེ་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ དུད་འགྲོའི་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ ཅིག་ ཀྱང་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ ཤར་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: That with together, animals' light green lustreless, one, also, wisdom's light with together dawned, then, comes.
sentences.i: Together with it, a dull green light of the animals also comes, dawning alongside the light of wisdom.
sentences.n: The dull light of the seventh day, the animals', which comes from delusion (007). cig kyang, 'one, also' (the other recension zhig). shar nas 'ong, 'comes having dawned'; the other recension has 'char du 'ong, 'comes to dawn'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཁྱོད་ བག་ཆགས་ འཁྲུལ་བའི་ དབང་ གིས༔ འོད་ ཁ་དོག་ ལྔ་ལྡན་ དེ་ ལ་ སྐྲག་ ཅིང་ བྲོས་ ནས༔ དུད་འགྲོའི་ འོད་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་སུ་ འོང་བས༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, you, habitual-tendencies delusion's power by, light colours five-having that at frightened and, fled, then; animals' light lustreless that to attached coming-because:
sentences.i: At that time, through the force of your deluded habitual tendencies, you will take fright at that light of five colours and flee from it, and come to be attached to the dull light of the animals. So
sentences.n: The print has དུད་འགྲེའི (dud 'gre'i), a misprint for དུད་འགྲོའི (dud 'gro'i), corrected here; the word stands rightly in the line above and twice on the next page, and the second stroke of the o may only be worn away on the block. bag chags 'khrul ba'i dbang gis, 'by the force of deluded habitual tendencies'. lnga ldan, 'having five', a short form of lnga dang ldan pa. skrag cing bros nas, 'afraid, and fleeing'. chags su 'ong bas, 'because you come to be attached', as in 007; it runs on to the commands.

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཁྱོད་ འོད་ ཁ་དོག་ ལྔ་ལྡན་ བཀྲག་མདངས་ཅན་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག་ ཡེ་ཤེས་སུ་ རང་ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: At-that-time, you, light colours five-having, lustre-radiance-having, that at not fear! Not be-afraid! As-wisdom own-face knowing do!
sentences.i: do not then fear that lustrous, radiant light of five colours; do not be afraid; recognise it as wisdom, your own nature.
sentences.n: The print writes de tsa na as de tsan (ཙན), a contraction written out here. bkrag mdangs can, 'having lustre and radiance'. ma 'jigs shig, ma skrag cig, two prohibitions; the print has no ༔ after the second, where the other recension has one. ye shes su rang ngo shes par gyis shig, 'recognise your own face as wisdom'.

sentences.w: འོད་ ཀྱི་ ནང་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཆོས་ ཀྱི་ རང་སྒྲ་ འབྲུག་ སྟོང་ དུས་ གཅིག་ ལ་ ལྡིར་བ་ ཙམ་ ཡོད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Light's inside all, reality's own-sound, thunders thousand time one-at booming as-much-as there-is.
sentences.i: Within the light, all through it, is the natural sound of reality, like a thousand thunders roaring at once.
sentences.n: The print runs rang sgra and 'brug together (སྒྲའབྲུག), a contraction written out here. chos kyi rang sgra, 'the own sound of reality', the sound that is reality's own and comes from nowhere else, as chos nyid kyi rang sgra in 003. 'brug, 'dragon', is also 'thunder', the dragon's voice; stong, 'a thousand'. ldir ba tsam, 'as much as roaring' (ldir, 'to boom, roar'). 'od kyi nang thams cad, 'all the inside of the light'; the other recension has 'od kyi nang nas thams cad, 'from within the light, all', and has no dus gcig la, 'at one time'. yod do, 'there is', where the other recension has 'ong, 'comes'.

sentences.w: སྒྲ་གྲགས་ ལ་ ལྡིར་ ཆེ་བ༔ འུར་སྒྲ་ བསོ་སྒྲ༔ སྐྲག་དངངས་ དྲག་པོ་ དང་ བཅས་ ནས་ འབྱུང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Sound loud and booming great, 'ur-sound, bso-sound, fright-terror fierce with together, then, arises.
sentences.i: Loud and booming, a din, a roar, it comes with fierce terror.
sentences.n: sgra grags la ldir che ba, 'loud of sound and great in booming': la between two qualities is 'and', as in gsal la dwangs pa; sgra grags is 'sound, noise' (grags, 'to sound, be heard'); the other recension has sgra drag, 'fierce sound'. 'ur sgra, 'a din, a roar'; bso sgra is not a word known to the drafter, and is taken as another cry of the kind, 'a roar'; the sense is not sure. skrag dngangs drag po dang bcas nas 'byung, 'it comes with fierce fright and terror', the terror the sounds bring; bcas[?]: the prefix b looks worn on the image, and the transcription and the other recension both have bcas. The other recension has sgra drag po'i drag sngags dang bcas nas 'ong, 'comes with the fierce mantras of fierce sound', which differs in sense: the mantras in the sound, not the terror it brings.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ བྲོས་ཤིག༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ རང་སྣང་ རིག་པའི་ རང་དུ་ རང་ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That at not fear! Not flee! You-yourself's own-appearance, knowing's own-as, own-face knowing do!
sentences.i: Do not fear it; do not flee; recognise it as your own appearance, awareness itself.
sentences.n: ma 'jigs shig, ma bros shig, 'do not fear, do not flee'; the other recension adds ma skrag cig, 'do not be afraid'. rang snang rig pa'i rang du, 'as own appearance, as awareness's own': rang du, 'as its own', is taken as 'as awareness itself'. The other recension has rig pa'i rang rtsal du ngo shes, 'recognise it as the natural energy of awareness'; rtsal may have dropped from the print, but its words give sense and are followed. rang is said four times: khyod rang, 'you yourself', rang snang, 'own appearance', rang du, and rang ngo, 'own face'.

sentences.w: དུད་འགྲོའི་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ ཆགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ ཞེན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Animals' light green lustreless that to not be-attached! Not cling!
sentences.i: Do not be attached to that dull green light of the animals; do not cling to it.
sentences.n: ma chags shig, ma zhen cig, 'do not be attached, do not cling', the pair of the days before.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་ ན་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་ གཏི་མུག་ དུད་འགྲོའི་ གནས་སུ་ སྐྱེས་ སྟེ༔ གླེན་ལྐུགས་ བཀོལ་གཅོད་ ཀྱི་ སྡུག་བསྔལ་ མཐའ་ ལས་ འདས་པ་ མྱོང་ སྟེ༔ ཐར་པའི་ དུས་ མི་ འབྱུང་བས་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ ཆགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That to attached if, as-for: you, delusion animals' place-in born, and: dumb-mute labour-slaughter's suffering edge from gone-beyond experiencing, and: liberation's time not arising-because, that to not be-attached!
sentences.i: If you are attached to it, you will be born in the animal realm of delusion and suffer the boundless misery of dullness and dumbness, of being worked and slaughtered, and the time of liberation will not come. So do not be attached to it.
sentences.n: gti mug dud 'gro'i gnas, 'the animal realm of delusion', the poison that leads there. skyes, 'born', the past stem of skye; the other recension has lhung, 'fall', 'fall into the realm'. glen lkugs, 'dull and mute' (glen, 'stupid'; lkugs, 'dumb'). bkol gcod: bkol, 'to put to work'; gcod, 'to cut'; taken as 'being worked and slaughtered'; the other recension has bkol spyod, 'being used as a beast of burden'. mtha' las 'das pa, 'gone beyond the limit', boundless. myong, 'to experience'. thar pa'i dus mi 'byung bas, 'because the time of liberation will not arise'; the other recension has thon pa'i dus, 'the time of getting out'.

sentences.w: འོད་ ཁ་དོག་ ལྔ་ལྡན་ གསལ་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ དེ་ ལ་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Light colours five-having, bright and shimmering, that to devotion do!
sentences.i: Turn with devotion to that light of five colours, bright and shimmering.
sentences.n: mos pa gyis shig, 'do devotion!', closes a sentence here; the other recension has gyis la, 'do, and', and runs on as on the days before.

sentences.w: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིག་འཛིན་ སློབ་དཔོན་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ ལ་ མདུན་ བརྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་ གཏོད་ ལ༔
sentences.l: The Blessed-One knowledge-holder master's deity-host to longing(?) one-pointedly direct, and:
sentences.i: Direct a single-minded longing to the host of deities of the Blessed One, the knowledge-holder master, and think:
sentences.n: slob dpon, 'master, teacher' (Sanskrit ācārya); the bcom ldan 'das rig 'dzin slob dpon, 'the Blessed One, the knowledge-holder master', is the chief of the knowledge-holders. mdun brtse gcig tu is kept as printed: the usual words are 'dun pa rtse gcig tu, 'with one-pointed longing' (005), which the other recension has. The print writes mdun brtse gcig here and again below; it had mdun pa in 003 and 007 too (beside 'dun pa in 002 and 004–006), so the m is one of its spellings, and brtse for rtse adds a prefix that makes the word 'love'. The sense is taken as 'dun pa rtse gcig tu.

sentences.w: རིག་འཛིན་ དཔའ་བོ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་ དང་ བཅས་པ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱིས༔ བདག་ དག་པ་ མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ ཀྱི་ གནས་སུ་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ བྱོན་པར་ འདུག་པས༔
sentences.l: 'Knowledge-holders, heroes, sky-goers with together (plural) by, me pure Sky-Faring's abode-to meeting for come are-because:
sentences.i: 'The knowledge-holders, with the heroes and the sky-goers, have come to welcome me to the pure Sky-Faring abode; so
sentences.n: The thought to be held begins here and runs to drang du gsol, closed by snyam pa'i, 'thinking', three units on. bdag, 'I, me', the humble word. bsu ba la byon par 'dug pas, 'since they have come to meet': byon, the past stem of 'byon, the respectful 'come'; 'dug after a verb, as in 007 (byon par 'dug gis). The other recension has rig 'dzin gyi lha tshogs dpa' bo mkha' 'gro ... 'di rnams, 'these hosts of knowledge-holder deities, heroes and sky-goers', and 'byon par, 'are coming', with the present stem.

sentences.w: ཁྱེད་ རྣམས་ མཁྱེན་ བདག་ ལྟ་བུའི་ སེམས་ཅན་ ཚོགས་ མ་ བསགས་པ༔ ད་ ཞག་ ཕན་ཆད་དུ་ དུས་གསུམ་ གྱི་ བདེ་གཤེགས་ རིགས་ལྔའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ དེ་ཙམ་ ཅིག་ གི་ ཐུགས་རྗེས་ བཟུང་ ཡང་ མ་ ཟིན་པ་ འདི༔ བདག་ འདྲ་བ་ ཨ་ཙ་མ་ར༔
sentences.l: you (plural) know! A-being like-me, accumulations not gathered, now-days up-to, three-times' sugatas five-families' deity-hosts so-many one's compassion-by held though, not caught, this; me-like, alas!
sentences.i: you know me: a being like me, who has gathered no accumulations; who until these days has been held by the compassion of so many deities of the five families of sugatas of the three times, and yet was not caught; one like me, alas!
sentences.n: The print has བདེ་གཤིགས (bde gshigs), a misprint for བདེ་གཤེགས (bde gshegs), corrected here; bde gshegs is short for bde bar gshegs pa, 'sugata' (007), which the other recension has. khyed rnams mkhyen, 'you (all) know', with mkhyen, the respectful 'know': the appeal of a prayer, 'take heed of me'; the other recension has re mkhyen, 'I rely on you, you know'. tshogs ma bsags pa, 'who has not gathered the accumulations', of merit and wisdom (bsags, the past stem of gsog, 'to gather': gsog / bsags / bsag / sogs). da zhag phan chad du, 'up to these days now' (da, 'now'; zhag, 'day'; phan chad du, 'up to'), the days of the bardo just past; the reading is not sure. dus gsum, 'the three times', past, present and future. de tsam cig gi, 'of so many', with thugs rjes, 'by the compassion'. bzung yang ma zin pa, 'held, yet not caught' (bzung, the past stem of 'dzin; zin, 'be caught'): the deities held him and he slipped away. The other recension has thugs rje'i 'od zer gyis bzung, 'held by the rays of compassion'. bdag 'dra ba, 'one like me'. a tsa ma ra is kept as printed: the usual cry of dismay is a tsa ma re, which the transcription has, but nothing stands over the r on the image; the other recension has a tsa ma. The sentence has no verb: it is a lament.

sentences.w: ད་ ནི་ རིག་འཛིན་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ ཁྱེད་ རྣམས་ ཀྱིས་ འདི་ མན་ཆད་ ཅི་ནས་ཀྱང་ མ་ བཏང་ཅིག༔ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུས་ བཟུང་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Now, as-for, knowledge-holders' deity-host, you (plural) by, this downward, by-any-means not let-go! Compassion's iron-hook-by hold!
sentences.i: Now, you hosts of knowledge-holder deities, from this time on do not let me go, whatever happens: hold me with the hook of your compassion!
sentences.n: The print has ཚོཌ (tshoḍ), a misprint for ཚོགས (tshogs), corrected here: lha tshogs, 'host of deities'; on the image the letter after tsho is not sure ([?]), one reversed-looking letter like ḍa with no s after it, but only tshogs gives sense. 'di man chad, 'from this on' (man chad, 'from … downward, from then on'); the other recension has nga 'di man chad du, 'me, from now on'. ci nas kyang, 'by any means at all'. ma btang cig, 'do not let go': btang is the past stem of gtong, where the other recension has the present, ma gtong zhig. thugs rje'i lcags kyus, 'by the iron hook of compassion', the hook of the days before; the print cuts the -gs of lcags as one sign (ལྕགྶ), written out here. bzung cig, 'hold!': bzung is the past stem of 'dzin, where the imperative is zung (the other recension zungs). The transcription of this print has sku for kyu; the image has kyu.

sentences.w: དག་པ་ མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ཞིང་དུ་ ད་ལྟ་ ཁོན་ ནས་ དྲང་དུ་ གསོལ༔ སྙམ་པའི་ མདུན་ བརྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་ གཏོད་ ལ་ སྨོན་ལམ་ འདི་སྐད་དུ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Pure Sky-Faring's realm-to now right-away(?) leading I-pray!' thinking's longing(?) one-pointedly direct, and: prayer these-words-in obtain(?)!
sentences.i: I pray you, lead me now, this very moment, to the pure Sky-Faring realm.' Direct a single-minded longing with that thought, and make this prayer:
sentences.n: khon nas is kept as printed. It is not a word the drafter knows; the other recension has da lta kho nar, 'this very moment', and the translation follows it; khon nas may be a slip for kho na nas; khong nas, 'from within, from the heart', is another possible reading. drang du gsol, 'I pray that you lead': drang is the future stem of 'dren, 'to lead' (the other recension drangs, the past). snyam pa'i, 'thinking', closes the thought. mdun brtse gcig tu as above. smon lam 'di skad du thob cig, read as before as a guess, 'make this prayer'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་མ་ རིག་འཛིན་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ རྣམས་ ཀྱང་ དགོངས་སུ་ གསོལ༔ / བརྩེ་བ་ ཆེན་པོས་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲང་དུ་ གསོལ༔ / བག་ཆགས་ དྲག་པོས་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པའི་ ཚེ༔ / ལྷན་སྐྱེས་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ གསལ་བའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ལ༔ / དཔའ་བོ་ རིག་འཛིན་ ཚོགས་ ཀྱི་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲོངས༔ / ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ མཁའ་འགྲོའི་ ཚོགས་ ཀྱིས་ རྒྱབ་ ནས་ སྐྱོར༔ / བར་དོ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ འཕྲང་ ལས་ བསྒྲལ་ ནས་ ཀྱང་༔ / དག་པ་ མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ དེ་རུ་ སྐྱོལ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Knowledge-holder deity-hosts (plural) also, heed I-pray!
Love great-by the-way leading I-pray!
Habitual-tendencies fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
coemergent wisdom bright's light-path on,
heroes, knowledge-holders, host's(?) the-way lead!
Mothers supreme, sky-goers' host by, from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage from having-freed, also,
pure Sky-Faring realm that-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! Hosts of knowledge-holder deities, I pray you, think of me;
I pray you, lead the way in your great love.
When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce habitual tendencies,
on the bright light-path of coemergent wisdom
may the host of heroes and knowledge-holders lead the way,
may the host of sky-goers, the supreme mothers, support me from behind;
and when you have freed me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo,
bring me to that pure Sky-Faring realm.
sentences.n: The prayer of the seventh day, on the pattern of the days before (007): nine syllables to the line after kyai ma, here in eight lines. dgongs su gsol, 'I pray, think (of me)': dgongs, the respectful 'think, have in mind'. brtse ba chen pos, 'by great love'. drang du gsol, 'I pray that you lead', and drongs, the imperative of 'dren, 'lead!'. lhan skyes, short for lhan cig skyes pa, 'coemergent'. dpa' bo rig 'dzin tshogs kyi lam sna drongs: the print has kyi, 'of', where the other recension has rnams kyis, 'by', marking the leaders, as mkha' 'gro'i tshogs kyis does in the next line; kyi is taken as standing for kyis, as the print elsewhere writes gi for gis (gcig gi in the pilot), and 005 read yi as yis in its prayer. Read as printed, it would be 'lead the way of the host'. yum mchog, 'supreme mothers', the consorts. skyor, 'support!', as in 007. bsgral nas kyang, 'and having freed', bsgral the past stem of sgrol. skyol, the imperative of skyel, 'bring!' (skyel / bskyal / bskyal / skyol). de ru, 'to that', ru after a vowel. The other recension writes kye ma for kyai ma and drangs for drang.

sentences.w: ཅེས་ མོས་གུས་ དྲག་པོས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ བཏབ་པས༔ རིག་འཛིན་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ རྣམས་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀར་ འཇའ་འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས༔ དག་པ་ མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ ཀྱི་ གནས་སུ་ སྐྱེ་བར་ ཐེ་ཚོམ་ མེད་དོ༔
sentences.l: So, devotion-respect fierce-by prayer made-because: knowledge-holder deity-hosts (plural)'s heart-into rainbow-light-as dissolving, then; pure Sky-Faring's abode-in being-born-as doubt there-is-not.
sentences.i: When the prayer is made in this way with fierce devotion, one dissolves as rainbow light into the hearts of the hosts of knowledge-holder deities, and is born, without any doubt, in the pure Sky-Faring abode.
sentences.n: ces, 'so (it says)', closes the words of the prayer. btab pas, 'because it was made', btab, the past stem of 'debs. 'ja' 'od du thim, 'to dissolve as rainbow light'. skye bar the tshom med do, 'there is no doubt of being born'.

sentences.w: དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་ གྱི་ རིགས་ ཐམས་ཅད་ འདི་ ནས་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་ དེ་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཤ་སྟག་གོ༔
sentences.l: Spiritual-friend's kinds all, here-from face meeting, and, freed, nothing-but.
sentences.i: All who are of the family of the spiritual friend recognise it here and are freed, every one.
sentences.n: dge ba'i bshes gnyen, 'spiritual friend, teacher of virtue' (Sanskrit kalyāṇamitra); dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rigs thams cad, 'all of the family of the spiritual friend', is taken as all who have followed such a teacher; the phrase is short and the sense is not sure. 'di nas, 'from here, at this point'. ngo 'phrod de, 'recognition comes, and'. sha stag, 'nothing but, all without exception', with -go closing the sentence after -g. The other recension has thams cad kyang, 'all, too'.

sentences.w: འདིར་ བག་ཆགས་ ངན་ ཡང་ གྲོལ་བར་ ངེས་སོ༔
sentences.l: Here, habitual-tendencies bad even freed-as certain.
sentences.i: Here even those of bad habitual tendencies are sure to be freed.
sentences.n: bag chags ngan, 'bad habitual tendencies', stands for those who have them; yang, 'even' (the other recension kyang). grol bar nges so, 'it is certain that they are freed'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡན་ཆད་ ནི་ འཆི་ཁའི་ བར་དོ་ ལ་ འོད་གསལ་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་པ་ དང༔ ཆོས་ཉིད་ ཞི་བའི་ བར་དོ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ཐོས་གྲོལ་ ཆེན་མོ་ ཐལ་ལོ༔
sentences.l: That above, as-for: death-point's between in clear-light face-meeting and; reality-itself peaceful's between face-introduced, Hearing-Liberation Great, finished(?).
sentences.i: All that stands above, the recognition of the clear light in the bardo of the moment of death and the pointing-out of the peaceful bardo of reality, the Great Liberation through Hearing, is finished.
sentences.n: The close of text kha, the text that began with the title in the pilot. de yan chad, 'that and everything above it' (yan chad, 'from … upward'). 'od gsal ngo 'phrod pa, 'the recognition of the clear light', with ngo 'phrod, the recognition that comes, against ngo sprad pa, 'the pointing-out', in the second item; the other recension has ngo sprad pa in both, and bar dor for bar do la. chos nyid zhi ba'i bar do, 'the peaceful bardo of reality', the bardo of the peaceful deities, the subject of the parts since 002. thal lo: thal is 'to pass through, to have gone by'; with the sentence-ending -lo it is taken as a closing word, 'it is finished, it has gone through'; the sense is not sure. The other recension has lags so, 'this is the Great Liberation through Hearing', and runs straight on into the wrathful deities, which this print sets out as a text of its own (ga). The print has no tsheg before the ༔ of dang.

sentences.l: Iti. Seal, seal, seal.
sentences.i: Thus. Sealed, sealed, sealed.
sentences.n: ཨྠྀི is one stack: ཨ (a) with ཐ (tha) under it, and two i-vowels above, a reversed gi-gu and a gi-gu, one for each letter. So it spells i-thi, Sanskrit iti, 'thus', the word that closes a Sanskrit text, written as one sign; treasure texts close with it. rgya, 'seal' (Sanskrit mudrā), three times: the threefold seal at the end of a treasure text, said to mark it as sealed in secrecy and entrusted; its meaning is explained in more than one way. A last ༔ stands faint against the frame. Text kha ends here, on p. 79, a page of three lines; the wrathful deities follow on the next leaf as text ga.
